tasks.short: File, check and keep personnel documents complete in AFAS dossiers: contracts, certificates, leave, evaluations, grievances.

today.trigger: A document arrives by mail, Teams, the agency portal or the paper tray of a site office.
steps: Open the attachment or scan and work out what it is and whose it is
Check it against the AFAS record (name, personnel number, dates, signatures)
Rename and upload it to the right AFAS dossier category
Update the matching fields (contract end, certificate expiry, leave dates)
Chase the sender when something is missing or unsigned
drudgery: Typing dates from PDFs into fields
today.time_sinks: Unclear or bundled scans from three sites, and missing signatures that need a second round.

lenses.faster: A model classifies each document, matches it to the employee and proposes the fields; the administrator checks a list instead of opening every PDF.
lenses.autonomous: Documents dropped in a shared HR mailbox or the Pocket app are read, filed and validated overnight; only mismatches land in an exceptions queue.
lenses.ambitious: Every dossier is audit-complete for all 1,200 employees and the seasonal flex pool, with a nightly completeness score per site.
lenses.joy: No more re-keying dates from scans; what remains is fixing real gaps and helping managers get it right.
lenses.options: For an ambiguous document the system shows the two or three likeliest employees and categories with its reasons.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the document-type catalogue, the validation rules and the exception queue rather than the filing itself.
reach: L&D Specialist: certificate expiry tracking for forklift, VCA and food safety
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: dossier data-quality reporting

tasks.human_edge: Grievances, performance evaluations and anything touching health need judgment about who may see what; the administrator decides filing and access for those.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured documents become structured fields inside a deterministic AFAS filing and validation flow, and the output is checkable against the record.

in_practice.trigger: New document in the HR intake mailbox, Pocket app upload or agency portal export.
steps: Model classifies the document type and extracts name, personnel number, dates and signature presence
Deterministic rules match it to the AFAS employee and check dates against contract and certificate data
Clean matches are filed and fields updated; mismatches and sensitive types (grievance, evaluation, medical) go to the exceptions queue
Administrator reviews the queue daily and approves or corrects
Missing-item reminders go out automatically to the sender
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves every exception and every sensitive document type; routine types are spot-checked weekly at 5%.
data_needed: AFAS dossier categories and employee master data
Sample of labelled historical documents for testing
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS dossier audit trail plus an intake log in SharePoint listing document, decision, confidence and reviewer.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 Jonas reads documents into dossier fields.
Document-to-fields extraction with validation and an exceptions queue fits records work at autonomy 4.
evidence.source: Research digest, 'For the model'; model knowledge

risks: Misfiled sensitive documents expose personal data (AVG breach)
Health details in documents reach model prompts (GDPR Art. 9)
No published error rate for Jonas extraction
research_questions: What extraction accuracy does Jonas reach on our contracts, ID copies and Studytube certificates over a 200-document sample?
Which share of incoming documents today is grievance, evaluation or medical and must bypass the model?
Does the works council see automated dossier filing as needing consent under WOR art. 27(1)(k)?

tasks.short: Type employee data into AFAS: address changes, absences, production figures, manager reports, exit dates and reasons.

today.trigger: An email, form or phone call reports a change, or a manager sends a list.
steps: Read the change request and find the employee in AFAS
Type the change into the right AFAS screen with a start date
Enter absence notifications passed on by shift leaders
Copy production or performance figures from site Excel sheets
Record exit date and reason from the termination letter
drudgery: Copying site Excel figures by hand
Entering absences phoned in by shift leaders
today.time_sinks: Changes arriving in many formats from three sites, and corrections after payroll spots a typo.

lenses.faster: Employees change their own address and bank details in AFAS Pocket, and site figures import from a fixed Excel template, so most typing disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Self-service changes and template imports post to AFAS through workflows with validation, triggered by the submission itself.
lenses.ambitious: Every change is live the same day, so the payroll month close starts with zero late mutations.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses re-keying; the administrator handles the odd case that rules cannot settle.
lenses.options: For each data stream the team can choose self-service, template import or manager form, and compare error rates.
lenses.altitude: The administrator designs the AFAS workflows and validation rules and watches the reject list.
reach: Payroll Specialist: pre-checking mutations before the month close
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: maintaining import templates

tasks.human_edge: Termination reasons and absence notes are sensitive; the administrator decides wording and makes sure no medical detail is recorded (Wet verbetering poortwachter and AVG).
tasks.pattern_why: Inputs are structured and the rules can be written down; AFAS workflows and validated imports do it without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Employee submits a change in AFAS Pocket, a manager submits an AFAS workflow form, or a site uploads the weekly figures template.
steps: AFAS workflow validates the input (postcode format, IBAN check, dates within contract)
Valid changes post directly; changes affecting pay are flagged for Payroll
Template import loads site production figures to the employee record
Rejects go to the administrator's exceptions list with the reason
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator handles rejects and approves exit records; payroll-affecting changes are checked by the Payroll Specialist before close.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS mutation history and workflow log.

evidence.claim: New hires and employees submit data through the AFAS Pocket app.
Validated self-service and template imports replace manual entry for structured HR data.

risks: Shift workers without easy app access keep using email, so manual entry lingers
Recording production per person may count as performance monitoring needing works council consent (WOR art. 27(1)(l))
Absence reasons with medical content entered by mistake
research_questions: What share of warehouse staff actively uses AFAS Pocket today?
How many payroll corrections per month trace back to manual entry errors?
Does the OR already have an agreement covering per-person production figures in AFAS?

tasks.short: Process hires, exits, leave, transfers and promotions in AFAS so contract, pay scale and payroll are right.

today.trigger: A manager email, a signed offer from Recruitee, or a resignation letter.
steps: Collect the details from the manager or HRBP
Check CAO scale, hours and contract type
Enter the event in AFAS with effective date
Create the letter or contract addendum from the SharePoint template
Inform payroll and the manager
drudgery: Copying offer data from Recruitee to AFAS
today.time_sinks: Incomplete requests and back-and-forth about scale, start date and hours.

lenses.faster: An agent pulls the offer or request, fills the AFAS mutation and drafts the letter; the administrator checks one screen.
lenses.autonomous: An accepted offer in Recruitee or an approved manager form starts the mutation, letter and payroll notice without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: Every personnel action is done within one working day, and ketenregeling and contract-end dates are never missed.
lenses.joy: The chase for missing fields goes; what stays is checking the CAO fit and helping the manager.
lenses.options: For promotions the agent shows the scale and step options under the CAO with cost per option for the HRBP.
lenses.altitude: The administrator maintains the event rules, templates and CAO tables the agent uses and reviews its output.
reach: Payroll Specialist: preparing payroll mutations
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: CAO scale checks

tasks.human_edge: Edge cases (ketenregeling, transitievergoeding, leave combined with illness) need someone who knows the CAO and the person; the administrator approves every mutation.
tasks.pattern_why: Several systems, templates and exceptions are involved, and a wrong mutation hits pay, so a person approves before it posts.

in_practice.trigger: Offer accepted in Recruitee, manager workflow approved in AFAS, or resignation logged.
steps: Agent gathers event data from Recruitee or the AFAS form and fills gaps by messaging the manager
Deterministic checks against CAO scale tables, contract history and ketenregeling
Agent prepares the AFAS mutation and drafts the letter from the SharePoint template
Administrator reviews and approves; mutation posts and payroll is notified
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves each mutation and letter before it posts or is sent.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS mutation history plus an agent action log in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: SixFifty drafts contracts and sends them for signature within strict workflows on an expert-maintained law base.
evidence.source: HR Dive press release, 13 Oct 2026 [S6] (US law only)

evidence.claim: Agents that prepare HR transactions with approval steps fit this work.

risks: Wrong scale or start date causes pay errors
Recruitee-AFAS field mapping drifts after updates
Templates out of date with CAO changes
research_questions: How many personnel actions per month, and what share needs a correction after posting?
Can Recruitee push offer data to AFAS through an existing connector?
Who owns CAO table updates and how fast after a new CAO?

tasks.short: Screen applications for basic eligibility: work permit, licences, certificates, availability for shifts.

today.trigger: New applications arrive in Recruitee or through an agency.
steps: Open each application and CV
Check knock-out criteria: right to work, driving licence C/CE and code 95, forklift certificate, shift availability
Mark the candidate in the Recruitee stage
Pass suitable candidates to the recruiter or hiring manager
drudgery: Reading CVs for the same few facts
today.time_sinks: Peak-season volume and CVs that do not state licences or availability clearly.

lenses.faster: A model lists per applicant which knock-out facts are stated, missing or unclear, with the quote from the CV.
lenses.autonomous: Missing facts trigger a polite question to the applicant through Recruitee; the decision stays with a person.
lenses.ambitious: Every applicant gets a response within two working days, even in peak season.
lenses.joy: Less skimming of CVs; more time on calls with candidates who fit.
lenses.options: The administrator sees a short summary next to the full CV and can sort by missing items.
lenses.altitude: The administrator, with the recruiters, defines the knock-out criteria per role and checks the summaries for bias.
reach: Recruiter: first-round phone screens
Recruiter: candidate status communication

tasks.human_edge: Selecting or rejecting a person is a decision with legal weight (GDPR Art. 22, EU AI Act high-risk from December 2027); a person makes it and can explain it.
tasks.pattern_why: Applicant evaluation must stay with a person; AI only summarises facts against stated criteria.

in_practice.trigger: Application enters the 'new' stage in Recruitee.
steps: Model extracts licences, certificates, right-to-work statement and availability with source quotes
Deterministic check against the role's knock-out list
Recruitee note shows stated, missing and unclear items
Administrator decides the stage move; questions for missing items are sent after review
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator or recruiter makes every advance or reject decision; no automatic rejections.
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate notes and stage history.

evidence.claim: Applicant screening becomes high-risk under EU AI Act Annex III 4(a) from 2 December 2027.
evidence.source: AI Act Annex III; Digital Omnibus [S10][S11]

evidence.claim: A decision cannot rest solely on automated processing.

risks: Summaries carry bias or miss non-standard CVs
Tool becomes high-risk AI in 2027 with conformity duties
Applicants unaware of AI use (transparency)
research_questions: What share of applications fails on knock-out criteria alone?
Does Recruitee offer a built-in AI summary and where is the data processed?
How does the works council want to be involved before applicant screening support goes live?

tasks.short: Answer staff questions on pay, leave, CAO rules, benefits and certificates by mail, Teams and at the desk.

today.trigger: An employee or manager mails, calls or walks in with a question.
steps: Read the question and work out the person's contract and site
Look up the CAO, policy on SharePoint or the AFAS record
Write the answer, often in Dutch and English
Forward to payroll or the HRBP when it is not a standard question
drudgery: Answering the same leave-balance and holiday-pay questions
today.time_sinks: Repeat questions around payslip day, holiday pay in May and the season peak.

lenses.faster: A Teams bot answers policy questions from owned content and quotes leave balances from AFAS directly.
lenses.autonomous: The bot answers around the clock for shift workers and opens a ticket with the profile attached when it cannot.
lenses.ambitious: Every employee, including flex workers, gets the answer for their own CAO and contract in their language.
lenses.joy: The repeat questions go; the administrator handles the real cases and writes good content.
lenses.options: The bot can give the short answer plus the policy page, and offer a call with HR.
lenses.altitude: The administrator becomes the owner of the HR knowledge base and the escalation queue.
reach: Payroll Specialist: payslip explanation questions
HR Business Partner: first-line policy questions from managers

tasks.human_edge: Questions about sickness, conflict or personal trouble need a person, and the bot must hand them over quickly and kindly.
tasks.pattern_why: Answers come from owned content with deterministic entitlement lookups, and unresolved questions escalate to a person.

in_practice.trigger: Employee asks a question in Teams or the HR mailbox.
steps: Bot discloses it is AI and identifies the employee
Deterministic lookup for personal entitlements (leave balance, contract hours)
Policy answer from curated SharePoint content per CAO and site
Ticket with profile and conversation goes to HR when not resolved or when the topic is sensitive
Administrator reviews answer samples and updates content weekly
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator handles all tickets and sensitive topics; content changes are approved by the content owner.
data_needed: CAO texts and policies in plain language
Leave and contract data from AFAS
in_practice.logs_to: Conversation log and ticket queue, with retention agreed with the works council.

evidence.claim: Coca-Cola Andina's HR agent serves 1,200 users a month, answers per contract and region, and escalates with the profile attached.
Chatbots alone saved about 3% of work hours; gains come from workflow redesign.
Employee-facing bots must disclose they are AI.

risks: Wrong answer on pay or leave taken as a commitment
Tone mistakes on sensitive topics
Works council consent needed when the bot reads the personnel file (WOR art. 27(1)(k))
research_questions: How many questions per month and what share are repeat policy questions?
Which languages do warehouse and flex staff need?
Will the OR consent to logging questions per employee, and for how long?

tasks.short: Handle hiring paperwork: contract, ID copy, tax form, AFAS record, preboarding and mandatory course enrolments.

today.trigger: Candidate accepts the offer in Recruitee.
steps: Create the contract from the SharePoint template and send for signature
Collect ID copy, loonheffingsverklaring and bank details
Create the employee in AFAS
Enrol the new hire in mandatory Studytube courses
Arrange day-one items with the manager
drudgery: Chasing signed forms and ID copies
today.time_sinks: Missing documents before day one and last-minute start date changes.

lenses.faster: Offer data flows to AFAS, the contract is drafted and the Pocket preboarding request goes out at once.
lenses.autonomous: Acceptance triggers contract, preboarding forms, Studytube enrolments and reminders; the administrator sees a status board.
lenses.ambitious: Every new hire has a complete dossier and certificates planned before day one, feeding the 90-day retention goal.
lenses.joy: No chasing forms; time goes to a proper welcome and helping managers prepare.
lenses.options: Several start-date and course plans can be shown to the manager to pick from.
lenses.altitude: The administrator designs the preboarding flow and checks completeness per hire.
reach: Recruiter: offer-to-start handover
L&D Specialist: mandatory course planning for new starters

tasks.human_edge: The hiring decision and the conversation with the new hire stay human; the ID check against the original document is a legal duty.
tasks.pattern_why: Multi-system steps with exceptions; the contract and AFAS record are approved by a person.

steps: Agent drafts the contract from template and offer data
Pocket preboarding request asks for ID, tax form and bank details
Jonas reads documents into the dossier; checks flag gaps
Studytube enrolments created per role (VCA, forklift, food safety)
Administrator approves contract and AFAS record
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves the contract before signature and verifies the ID.

evidence.claim: AFAS lets new hires submit data in Pocket before day one; Jonas reads documents into fields.
SixFifty sends contracts for signature and distributes new-hire notices.

risks: ID-copy handling breaches AVG retention rules
Wrong template or CAO for the role
New hires not using Pocket
research_questions: What share of new hires has a complete dossier on day one today?
Is there a Recruitee-AFAS connector in use?
How many mandatory certificates are missing at day one?

tasks.short: Look up employee files to answer questions and prepare personnel actions, such as employer statements and contract checks.

today.trigger: Request from a manager, payroll, an employee or a bank.
steps: Find the employee in AFAS
Read through dossier documents for the facts
Check contract history, salary and dates
Write the answer or employer statement
Send after checking
today.time_sinks: Old scans and long contract histories.

lenses.faster: A dossier summary and contract timeline are ready in seconds, with links to sources.
lenses.autonomous: Standard statements are drafted from AFAS data when the request comes in.
lenses.ambitious: Contract-end and ketenregeling checks run for every employee each month, not only on request.
lenses.joy: Less searching; more time for the conversation behind the request.
lenses.options: Several draft answers or statement versions for the administrator to pick.
lenses.altitude: The administrator defines standard statements and checks the source data.
reach: HR Business Partner: preparing case files for personnel decisions

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what can be shared with whom and signing employer statements stays with a person.
tasks.pattern_why: Combines lookups across records with drafting, and outward statements need approval.

in_practice.trigger: Request in HR mailbox or Teams.
steps: Identify employee and requester rights
Pull AFAS data and summarise dossier with sources
Draft answer or statement
Administrator approves and sends
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves every outward answer and statement.

evidence.claim: Personal data lookups should be deterministic and quoted, not generated.

risks: Sharing data with someone without the right
Summary misses a key document
research_questions: Which request types are most frequent?
Can access rules per requester be enforced technically in AFAS?

tasks.short: Chase managers, sites, agencies and employees for missing records: signed forms, certificates, hours, evaluations.

today.trigger: A missing item is noticed, often at month close or audit.
steps: Make a list of missing items in Excel
Mail or Teams the manager, site or agency
Follow up when no answer
Receive and file the item
drudgery: Keeping chase lists up to date
today.time_sinks: Slow replies from busy shift managers and agencies.

lenses.faster: Missing items are found by a nightly check and reminders go out automatically.
lenses.autonomous: An agent nudges owners on a schedule and escalates after set days.
lenses.ambitious: Records complete for every employee and flex worker at all times.
lenses.joy: No chase spreadsheets; only true escalations need the administrator.
lenses.options: Reminder by Teams, mail or manager dashboard.
lenses.altitude: The administrator sets the completeness rules and escalation paths.
reach: Bookkeeper: matching agency hours to invoices
L&D Specialist: certificate chasing

tasks.human_edge: Escalating to a manager's boss or an agency account manager needs tact and relationships.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps and parties; the person handles escalations.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly completeness check finds a gap.
steps: Check rules flag missing items
Agent sends reminders to owner
Received items are read and filed
Unanswered items escalate to the administrator
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator decides on escalations beyond the owner.
in_practice.logs_to: Chase log in SharePoint and Power BI completeness dashboard.

risks: Reminder fatigue among managers
Agency data in portals not exportable
research_questions: How many items are chased per month?
Do agency portals offer exports or APIs?

role.altitude: From doing the records and answering questions to owning HR data quality, the HR knowledge base and the exception queue.
reach: Payroll Specialist: mutation checks before month close
Recruiter: offer-to-start handover
L&D Specialist: certificate tracking
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: data quality and import templates
Bookkeeper: agency hours checks
role.ceiling_note: About 730 of 1,600 hours per FTE sit in these tasks; roughly half can come back. The limits are AFAS data quality, works council consent, health-data rules and the judgment cases.
skills_to_grow: AVG and works council basics for AI
role.ambitious_version: Every dossier complete on day one, every question answered within minutes in the employee's language, and the two administrators running the system that does it.
